data.narrative:
Cache Energy is a Seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Arpit Dwivedi that has raised $8.5M to date. The valuation universe for comparison includes one public peer (LNZA) and eight private companies in the Climate & Energy sector, including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen.

The Stage-Progression method is the applicable triangulation approach here. Using total capital raised ($8.5M) as a baseline proxy and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier from Seed to the next financing stage yields an implied valuation of $21M. The Peer-Median method was not applied because the Climate & Energy universe lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables meeting minimum thresholds; while nine same-sector peers exist, fewer than three meet tight filtering criteria on stage and valuation tier, making a narrow peer median unreliable.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $18M (low) to $24M (high), with a median point of $21M. This range reflects conservative application of stage-progression mechanics rather than peer cross-validation. Key uncertainties include (1) the representativeness of the 2.5x multiplier for this specific subsector and company profile, and (2) the lack of contemporaneous Seed-stage Climate & Energy comparables to validate the step-up assumption. Additional funding milestones or revenue traction would strengthen conviction in any point estimate within this band.
